topic: UI Components, Design Patterns, and Design Systems
learningObjectives: Identify common UI components and their appropriate use cases.
Understand how reusable components create interface consistency.
Recognize common component states and interaction patterns.
Assemble a basic design system from reusable UI elements.

activities.title: UI Component Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the anatomy of common interface components.

content.concept: Components such as buttons, inputs, cards, navigation, dialogs, and dropdowns provide reusable interaction patterns.
content.tip: Explore each component to understand its structure and purpose.

descriptions: Triggers a primary or secondary action.
Allows users to enter or edit information.
Helps users move between sections or screens.
Displays important information or requests an action.
Allows users to select from a list of options.

activities.title: Component Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each user need with the most appropriate UI component.

content.concept: Selecting familiar components reduces interaction complexity and makes interfaces easier to understand.
content.tip: Choose the component that directly supports the user's task.

activities.title: Component States Lab
activities.instruction: Explore how a component changes across different interaction states.

content.concept: Components commonly have states such as default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, selected, and error.
content.tip: Observe how each state communicates what the user can do and what the system is doing.

descriptions: Appears when the pointer is positioned over the component.
Indicates that the component is currently being activated.
Shows that the action is temporarily unavailable.
Communicates that an operation is in progress.
Communicates that an input or operation has a problem.

activities.title: Mini Design System Builder
activities.instruction: Assemble the essential parts of a basic design system.

content.concept: A design system combines reusable components, design tokens, styles, states, and usage rules to maintain consistency.
content.tip: Build the system from foundational styles toward reusable components.

separation.learning: Teach the concept through an interactive experience.
